chunks: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام brought out Shurāḥah al-Hamdāniyyah, and the people nearly killed one another because of the crowding. So when he saw that, he ordered that she be taken back until the crowd lessened. Then she was brought out again, and the gate was closed.
He said: Then they stoned her until she died. Then he ordered concerning the gate, and it was opened. He said: Then whoever entered began cursing her.

He said: So when he saw that, he called out through his caller: O people, withhold your tongues from her, for no hadd punishment is carried out except that it becomes an expiation for that sin, just as a debt is repaid by a debt.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: The title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful.
key_terms.الزِّحَامِ: Overcrowding or pressing of people in a gathered crowd.
key_terms.حَدٌّ: A prescribed legal punishment in sacred law.
key_terms.فَرَمَوْهَا: They pelted her with stones, referring here to stoning.
key_terms.يَلْعَنُهَا: They were cursing her after the punishment.

ai.seo_question: Does the enforcement of a hadd punishment expiate the sin in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration describes the execution of the hadd punishment by stoning in the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and his management of the crowd during its enforcement. It also states that once the legal punishment has been carried out, it serves as expiation for the sin, so people are instructed not to continue reviling the punished person.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4995 - The Commander of the Faithful (as) brought out Shuraha Al-Hamdaniyyah, and the crowd became so dense that people were almost killing one another due to the overcrowding. When Imam (as) saw this, Imam (as) ordered her to be taken back until the crowd dispersed.
Then she was brought out again, and the gate was closed.

Imam (as) said: "They stoned her until she died."
Afterward, Imam (as) commanded that the gate be opened, and whoever entered began cursing her.

When Imam (as) observed this, Imam (as) called out through his announcer,
"O' people! Restrain your tongues from her, for no punishment is carried out except that it serves as atonement for that sin, just as a debt is repaid by a debt."
